caption: A burning sheet of newspaper is held up inside a fireplace opening, and its flames are pulled upward into the chimney.

sa.check: A burning sheet of newspaper is held inside a fireplace opening.
The flames bend upward toward the flue.
The smoke goes up the chimney.
The paper is consumed from its burning edge inward.
The flames do not lean out into the room.
The paper blackens behind the flame front.

pc.expect: The flames and smoke go upward into the flue rather than out into the room or downward.
pc.fail: The flames lean out into the room away from the flue; or the smoke pours into the room and sinks to the hearth; or the flames point downward at the hearth; or the smoke hangs as a fixed shape without rising.

pc.expect: The flames lean toward the flue where the draught pulls them and keep that lean while the sheet is held in the opening.
pc.fail: The flames lean toward the room's open side against the draught; or the flames' lean swings about while the sheet is held still and nothing else moves; or the flames stand dead straight while the smoke is drawn hard up the flue; or the flames lean out before the sheet is in the opening.

pc.expect: The burn advances from the burning edge into unburnt paper and the blackened paper stays black.
pc.fail: Blackened paper turns white again; or the flame front retreats leaving unburnt paper behind it; or the sheet grows as it burns; or the paper catches at a spot no flame reached.

pc.expect: The burning paper curls, blackens and thins and its ash flakes away; it does not melt or drip.
pc.fail: The paper melts and runs like plastic; or stays flat and white while flames sit on it; or turns to ash without ever blackening or curling; or the sheet stiffens into a board as it burns.

pc.expect: One sheet held in one fireplace; the paper shrinks to ash rather than vanishing while whole.
pc.fail: The sheet vanishes in a single frame while still large; or a second sheet appears already burning; or ash appears on the hearth with none falling there; or the sheet passes through the fireplace's back wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The fireplace's surround, the hearth and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The surround changes colour; or the hearth changes pattern; or items in the room rearrange.

note: Whoever holds the sheet is not judged.
